ANC & Medical Care.question: 1) The primary objective of antenatal care (ANC) is to:
ANC & Medical Care.option1: Ensure the health of both mother and fetus
ANC & Medical Care.exp: ANC aims to achieve the best possible outcome for both mother and baby through prevention, early detection, and management of complications.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 2) The World Health Organization (WHO) currently recommends a minimum of how many antenatal contacts for an uncomplicated pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: WHO recommends at least 8 antenatal contacts to improve maternal and perinatal outcomes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 3) The first antenatal visit should ideally occur:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Early booking allows timely screening, dating, counseling, and identification of high-risk pregnancies.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 4) A pregnant woman with chronic hypertension is classified as having:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Chronic hypertension increases maternal and fetal complications, making the pregnancy high risk.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 5) The most accurate method for estimating gestational age in the first trimester is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: First-trimester crown-rump length provides the most accurate gestational age assessment.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 6) At the first antenatal visit, all of the following are routinely recommended except:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: CT scanning is not a routine investigation during pregnancy because of fetal radiation exposure.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 7) The most common nutritional deficiency during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Iron deficiency is the commonest nutritional deficiency and the leading cause of anemia in pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 8) Routine iron supplementation during pregnancy primarily prevents:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Iron supplementation replenishes maternal iron stores and reduces the risk of iron deficiency anemia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 9) Routine folic acid supplementation during early pregnancy primarily reduces the risk of:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Periconceptional folic acid significantly reduces neural tube defects such as spina bifida.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 10) The recommended daily folic acid dose for a low-risk woman before conception and during early pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Women at average risk should receive 0.4 mg (400 µg) folic acid daily before conception and during the first trimester.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 11) Hyperemesis gravidarum is characterized by:
ANC & Medical Care.option1: Severe vomiting with dehydration and weight loss
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Hyperemesis gravidarum causes persistent vomiting leading to dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, and weight loss.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 12) The most common electrolyte abnormality in hyperemesis gravidarum is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Persistent vomiting results in sodium and potassium depletion.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 13) The first-line management of hyperemesis gravidarum includes:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Rehydration, correction of electrolyte imbalance, and antiemetic therapy are the mainstays of treatment.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 14) A pregnant woman with persistent vomiting should receive which vitamin before intravenous dextrose?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Thiamine should be administered before dextrose to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 15) A blood pressure of ≥140/90 mmHg first detected after 20 weeks of gestation without proteinuria is diagnostic of:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Gestational hypertension develops after 20 weeks in a previously normotensive woman without proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 16) The hallmark feature distinguishing preeclampsia from gestational hypertension is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Preeclampsia is defined by hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or evidence of end-organ dysfunction.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 17) The definitive treatment of preeclampsia is:
ANC & Medical Care.option3: Delivery of the fetus and placenta
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Delivery is the only definitive cure, although timing depends on gestational age and disease severity.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 18) The anticonvulsant of choice for prevention and treatment of eclamptic seizures is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Magnesium sulfate is superior to other anticonvulsants for preventing and controlling eclamptic seizures.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 19) Which antihypertensive is commonly used for acute severe hypertension in pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Intravenous or oral labetalol is a first-line agent for acute severe hypertension during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 20) Which antihypertensive drug is contraindicated during pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: ACE inhibitors such as enalapril are contraindicated because they can cause fetal renal damage and other congenital abnormalities.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 21) HELLP syndrome stands for:
ANC & Medical Care.option3: Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelet count
ANC & Medical Care.option4: Hemorrhage, Elevated Leukocytes, Low Plasma proteins
ANC & Medical Care.exp: HELLP syndrome is a severe variant of preeclampsia associated with significant maternal morbidity.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 22) The most common cause of anemia during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Iron deficiency accounts for the majority of anemia cases during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 23) According to WHO, anemia in pregnancy is defined as hemoglobin less than:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: WHO defines anemia in pregnancy as a hemoglobin concentration below 11 g/dL.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 24) The investigation of choice to confirm iron deficiency anemia is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Serum ferritin is the most sensitive indicator of depleted iron stores.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 25) Parenteral iron therapy is indicated when:
ANC & Medical Care.option1: Oral iron is ineffective or not tolerated
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Intravenous iron is preferred when oral therapy fails, is not tolerated, or rapid correction is needed.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 26) The commonest physiological cause of anemia during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Plasma volume increases proportionately more than red cell mass, causing physiological anemia of pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 27) Gestational diabetes mellitus is defined as:
ANC & Medical Care.option3: Glucose intolerance first recognized during pregnancy
ANC & Medical Care.exp: GDM refers to glucose intolerance first detected during pregnancy, regardless of whether it persists postpartum.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 28) Screening for gestational diabetes is routinely performed at:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Universal screening is generally recommended between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 29) The investigation of choice for diagnosing gestational diabetes is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: The OGTT is the standard diagnostic test for gestational diabetes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 30) The most common fetal complication of maternal diabetes is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Maternal hyperglycemia causes fetal hyperinsulinemia, leading to excessive fetal growth.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 31) The most common congenital anomaly associated with pregestational diabetes is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Congenital heart defects are the most frequent congenital malformations seen in infants of mothers with pregestational diabetes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 32) Which congenital anomaly is classically associated with maternal diabetes?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Sacral agenesis (caudal regression syndrome) is a classic, though uncommon, anomaly strongly associated with maternal diabetes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 33) The drug of choice for glycemic control in type 1 diabetes during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Insulin remains the standard treatment for women with type 1 diabetes during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 34) The physiological cardiovascular change during pregnancy includes:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Cardiac output increases by approximately 30–50% during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 35) The most common valvular heart disease encountered during pregnancy worldwide is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Rheumatic mitral stenosis remains the commonest significant valvular lesion complicating pregnancy in many developing countries.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 36) The New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification is used to assess:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: NYHA functional classification is widely used to evaluate cardiac status in pregnant women with heart disease.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 37) The most common bacterial cause of asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: E. coli is responsible for the majority of urinary tract infections during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 38) Untreated asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy predisposes to:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Untreated asymptomatic bacteriuria significantly increases the risk of acute pyelonephritis during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 39) The investigation of choice for confirming asymptomatic bacteriuria is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: A midstream urine culture is the gold standard for diagnosing bacteriuria in pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 40) Which infection in pregnancy is best prevented by administering anti-D immunoglobulin to an Rh-negative mother?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Anti-D immunoglobulin prevents maternal sensitization to Rh-positive fetal red blood cells, thereby preventing Rh isoimmunization.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 41) Routine administration of anti-D immunoglobulin is indicated in an unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant woman at approximately:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis is administered at around 28 weeks and again after delivery if the baby is Rh-positive.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 42) The purpose of administering anti-D immunoglobulin is to:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Anti-D destroys Rh-positive fetal red cells before the mother develops anti-D antibodies.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 43) The investigation used to detect fetomaternal hemorrhage after delivery is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: The Kleihauer-Betke test estimates the volume of fetomaternal hemorrhage to guide anti-D dosage.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 44) The screening test for maternal Rh antibodies is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: The indirect Coombs test detects circulating maternal anti-D antibodies.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 45) The definitive diagnosis of HIV infection during pregnancy is made by:
ANC & Medical Care.option1: Confirmatory HIV test according to national algorithm
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Positive screening tests require confirmation according to approved diagnostic algorithms.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 46) The risk of mother-to-child transmission of HIV is markedly reduced by:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Maternal ART is the most effective intervention for preventing vertical transmission of HIV.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 47) The most common cause of jaundice during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Viral hepatitis is the commonest cause of jaundice complicating pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 48) Hepatitis E infection during pregnancy is associated with:
ANC & Medical Care.option4: Chronic carrier state in all patients
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Hepatitis E is particularly severe during pregnancy, especially in the third trimester.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 49) The most common thyroid disorder during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Hypothyroidism is more common than hyperthyroidism in pregnancy and requires appropriate treatment.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 50) The drug of choice for treating hypothyroidism during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Levothyroxine is safe and is the standard treatment for maternal hypothyroidism.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 51) The drug of choice for hyperthyroidism during the first trimester is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: PTU is preferred during the first trimester because it has a lower risk of teratogenicity than methimazole/carbimazole.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 52) Radioactive iodine is contraindicated during pregnancy because it:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Radioiodine crosses the placenta and can ablate the fetal thyroid.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 53) The most common cause of thrombocytopenia during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Gestational thrombocytopenia accounts for approximately 75% of thrombocytopenia cases in pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 54) The most common inherited thrombophilia associated with recurrent pregnancy loss is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Factor V Leiden is the commonest inherited thrombophilia linked to venous thromboembolism and adverse pregnancy outcomes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 55) Pregnancy is considered a:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Pregnancy increases clotting factors and reduces fibrinolysis, predisposing to thromboembolism.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 56) The leading direct cause of maternal death worldwide is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Obstetric hemorrhage remains the leading direct cause of maternal mortality globally.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 57) The commonest indirect cause of maternal death in developing countries is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Severe anemia contributes substantially to indirect maternal mortality in low-resource settings.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 58) The most effective method of preventing neural tube defects is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Folic acid should ideally begin before conception and continue through the first trimester.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 59) Which vaccine is routinely recommended during pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Tetanus-containing vaccines are routinely recommended during pregnancy to protect both mother and newborn.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 60) The best indicator of adequate antenatal care is:
ANC & Medical Care.option3: Early booking with regular scheduled antenatal visits
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Early registration and regular ANC visits enable timely screening, prevention, and management of maternal and fetal complications.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 61) Which of the following is not a feature of severe preeclampsia?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: This is consistent with gestational hypertension, not severe preeclampsia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 62) The drug of choice for prevention of recurrent eclamptic convulsions is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Magnesium sulfate is superior to other anticonvulsants for preventing recurrent seizures in eclampsia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 63) The antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Intravenous calcium gluconate reverses magnesium toxicity.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 64) Loss of which clinical sign is the earliest indicator of magnesium sulfate toxicity?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Disappearance of deep tendon reflexes is the earliest clinical sign of magnesium toxicity.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 65) The most serious complication of magnesium sulfate toxicity is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Respiratory depression may progress to respiratory arrest if toxicity is not recognized promptly.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 66) The most common symptom of preeclampsia is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Persistent headache is the commonest presenting symptom of severe preeclampsia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 67) Pain in the right upper quadrant or epigastrium in preeclampsia suggests:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Hepatic ischemia and stretching of Glisson’s capsule produce epigastric or right upper quadrant pain.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 68) The drug of choice for long-term control of chronic hypertension during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Methyldopa has a long record of safety and remains a recommended antihypertensive during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 69) Which antihypertensive should never be used during pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are fetotoxic and contraindicated during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 70) The definitive diagnosis of eclampsia requires:
ANC & Medical Care.option3: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures in a woman with preeclampsia
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Eclampsia is defined by unexplained generalized seizures occurring in association with preeclampsia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 71) The most common cause of maternal death in eclampsia is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Intracranial hemorrhage and stroke are major causes of maternal mortality in eclampsia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 72) The most common cause of fetal death in severe preeclampsia is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Uteroplacental insufficiency leads to fetal hypoxia, growth restriction, and fetal demise.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 73) Which of the following is an indication for blood transfusion in pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Blood transfusion is reserved for severe anemia with symptoms or when rapid correction is required.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 74) The most common cause of megaloblastic anemia during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Folate deficiency is the commonest cause of megaloblastic anemia in pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 75) The investigation that best differentiates iron deficiency anemia from thalassemia trait is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Hemoglobin electrophoresis confirms thalassemia by identifying abnormal hemoglobin fractions.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 76) The commonest cause of pyelonephritis during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: E. coli is responsible for the majority of upper and lower urinary tract infections during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 77) The gold standard investigation for diagnosing urinary tract infection in pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Midstream urine culture identifies the organism and confirms significant bacteriuria.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 78) Asymptomatic bacteriuria during pregnancy should be:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Treatment reduces the risk of acute pyelonephritis and adverse pregnancy outcomes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 79) The safest imaging modality for fetal assessment during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Ultrasound is safe, non-ionizing, and the imaging modality of choice during pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 80) The most common cause of antepartum hospitalization in the first trimester is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Severe hyperemesis requiring intravenous fluids and electrolyte correction is the leading cause of first-trimester hospital admission.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 81) A pregnant woman develops generalized tonic-clonic convulsions at 36 weeks’ gestation with BP 170/110 mmHg. The most likely diagnosis is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: New-onset generalized seizures in a woman with preeclampsia are diagnostic of eclampsia after excluding other neurological causes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 82) Which of the following is the strongest risk factor for preeclampsia?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: A previous pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia markedly increases the risk of recurrence.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 83) Low-dose aspirin is recommended in women at high risk of preeclampsia because it:
ANC & Medical Care.option1: Reduces the risk of developing preeclampsia
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Low-dose aspirin started early in pregnancy reduces the incidence of preeclampsia in high-risk women.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 84) The most common symptom of hyperemesis gravidarum is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Hyperemesis gravidarum presents with intractable vomiting leading to dehydration and weight loss.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 85) Which of the following is a recognized risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Previous delivery of a macrosomic infant is an important risk factor for gestational diabetes.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 86) The investigation of choice for fetal anemia due to Rh isoimmunization is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity is the preferred non-invasive method for detecting fetal anemia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 87) Which of the following conditions requires anti-D immunoglobulin in an unsensitized Rh-negative woman?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Anti-D prophylaxis is indicated after any potentially sensitizing event involving fetomaternal hemorrhage.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 88) The physiological increase in plasma volume during pregnancy is approximately:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Plasma volume increases by about 40–50%, contributing to physiological hemodilution.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 89) The safest analgesic for fever or mild pain during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Paracetamol is the preferred analgesic and antipyretic during pregnancy when used in recommended doses.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 90) A pregnant woman with hypertension, proteinuria, elevated liver enzymes, and thrombocytopenia most likely has:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: The triad of Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, and Low Platelet count defines HELLP syndrome, a severe complication of preeclampsia.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 91) Which of the following physiological changes increases the risk of urinary tract infection during pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Progesterone-induced smooth muscle relaxation and mechanical compression by the uterus cause urinary stasis, predisposing to UTI.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 92) The preferred position for a pregnant woman after 20 weeks to avoid supine hypotensive syndrome is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: The left lateral position relieves compression of the inferior vena cava and improves uteroplacental blood flow.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 93) Supine hypotensive syndrome is caused primarily by compression of the:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Compression of the inferior vena cava decreases venous return, resulting in hypotension.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 94) Which of the following physiological respiratory changes occurs during pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Pregnancy increases tidal volume and minute ventilation under the influence of progesterone.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 95) The physiological increase in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) during pregnancy is approximately:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: GFR rises by approximately 40–50%, leading to lower serum creatinine concentrations in normal pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 96) Which of the following is a physiological hematological change in pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Pregnancy is a hypercoagulable state characterized by increased fibrinogen and several clotting factors.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 97) The routine screening test for syphilis during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: VDRL or RPR is the standard screening test, with treponemal tests used for confirmation.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 98) The drug of choice for treating syphilis during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Penicillin is the only proven treatment that effectively treats both maternal infection and prevents congenital syphilis.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 99) Which maternal infection is most strongly associated with congenital cataract?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Congenital rubella syndrome classically includes cataract, congenital heart disease, and sensorineural deafness.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 100) Which of the following vaccines is contraindicated during pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Live attenuated vaccines, including rubella, are contraindicated during pregnancy because of the theoretical risk to the fetus.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 101) The most common cause of maternal mortality among women with pre-existing heart disease during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Cardiac decompensation leading to heart failure is the leading cause of maternal death in pregnant women with significant heart disease.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 102) Which pregnant woman should receive high-dose folic acid (5 mg/day) before conception and during early pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.option4: Woman with a previous baby affected by a neural tube defect
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Women at high risk of neural tube defects should receive 5 mg folic acid daily beginning before conception.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 103) The physiological increase in maternal heart rate during pregnancy is approximately:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Maternal heart rate normally increases by about 10–20 beats/min because of increased metabolic demands.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 104) Which of the following is a contraindicated antihypertensive during breastfeeding as well as pregnancy due to fetal toxicity?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated during pregnancy because they can cause fetal renal dysgenesis and oligohydramnios.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 105) The best screening test for hepatitis B infection during pregnancy is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: HBsAg is the routine antenatal screening test used to identify hepatitis B infection.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 106) The newborn of an HBsAg-positive mother should receive:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Both hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulin should be administered as soon as possible after birth to reduce vertical transmission.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 107) The physiological leukocytosis of pregnancy is mainly due to an increase in:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Pregnancy normally causes neutrophilic leukocytosis, particularly during labor.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 108) Which of the following is not a physiological change during normal pregnancy?
ANC & Medical Care.exp: GFR increases by about 40–50% during normal pregnancy.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 109) The most common indication for antenatal hospitalization in the third trimester is:
ANC & Medical Care.exp: Severe preeclampsia frequently requires hospital admission for close maternal and fetal monitoring.

ANC & Medical Care.question: 110) The most important goal of antenatal care is:
ANC & Medical Care.option1: To increase the rate of hospital delivery
ANC & Medical Care.option2: To reduce the duration of labor
ANC & Medical Care.option3: To ensure a healthy mother and healthy baby by identifying and managing risks early
ANC & Medical Care.exp: The ultimate objective of antenatal care is early detection, prevention, and management of maternal and fetal complications, resulting in the best possible pregnancy outcome.
